manifest.contractionPolicy: adaptive (contraction, de+contraction): contraction uses the existing adaptive shrink rule, never growing, only after the delay; the production highDiversityThreshold is 0.8 but a 3-seed pilot showed 1.3-2.3 species per 24 creatures so the shrink branch never fired; the study sets contractionHighDiversityThreshold to 0, so the rule contracts on every post-delay plateau, bounded below by minPopulationFraction 0.5; the rule's low-diversity grow branch is disabled (lowDiversityThreshold 0) because it is checked first and would pre-empt the shrink; linear (lpsr, de+lpsr): the paper's budget-aware delayed L-SHADE linear population-size reduction, held at the base size until contractionDelayFraction of the record budget, then linear to lpsrMinPopulationSize (4, L-SHADE's N_min) at budget exhaustion, never growing; the paper's own delay cap value was not obtained
manifest.budgetPolicy: two phases. Primary (validationSeeds): records charged held equal, holdout and diversity probe uncharged, wall-clock measured. Equal-wall-clock (wallClockPhase): every arm gets the same per-run wall-clock cap, checked before every evaluation and before every refinement candidate, so no evaluation starts after the deadline, on fresh seeds, with the record budget raised tenfold so the clock is what stops each run; a run that ends with no scored candidate is recorded as censored and left out of every paired statistic; contraction schedules read the elapsed share of the wall-clock as budget progress. The wall-clock phase is not bit-reproducible, because the clock is real, so its arm order is rotated per seed to spread machine-load drift across arms

paper.title: Hybrid metaheuristics for architectural design optimization under small evaluation and wall-clock budgets
paper.author: Luciano Ambrosini
paper.sourcesRead: search-engine excerpts of the abstract page and the PDF text, retrieved 2026-11-16; direct fetches of arxiv.org (abs and pdf) were refused by the container proxy, so the full text was not read
pinned: MERLIN: CMA-ES whose sampling is enriched with differential-evolution trial vectors added as extra offspring; removing them leaves CMA-ES with the same initial step size
RAPTOR: particle swarm with success-history parameter adaptation, differential-evolution injection and local refinement
L-SHADE-SW: L-SHADE with an interleaved Solis-Wets local search whose result replaces the worst population member
budget-aware delay of L-SHADE linear population-size reduction (section 3.3, figure 2): improves three adaptive DE variants in 40 of 51 comparisons with no loss
budget: hard cap of 1,200 evaluations, all counted; the finite-element problem runs at equal wall-clock (15 minutes per run)
ablations: the gain is attributed to the DE injection; local search pays off only when its result re-enters the population
notPinned: the delay formula and delay cap value
the DE variant, F and CR used for injection
the injection fraction (this study uses the issue's 20%)
Solis-Wets step parameters (this study uses Gaussian perturbation of every weight)
